items.title: Global Summits 2025-26 — G20, BRICS, SCO, QUAD
items.body:
## G20
- **2025 — Johannesburg (20th):** first G20 summit ever held in **Africa**.
- **2026 — Miami, USA (21st):** planned for **14-15 December 2026** at Trump National Doral, chaired by **Donald Trump**. The US announced (Nov 2025) that **South Africa would not be invited**.
- The **African Union** became a permanent G20 member during India's 2023 presidency.

## BRICS
- **India holds the 2026 Chairship**, theme **'Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability'**.
- Bloc expansion: **Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, UAE (2024)** and **Indonesia (2025)** joined; acronym coined by Jim O'Neill (2001); first summit Russia (2009).

## SCO
- **2026 under China's presidency**; SCO established 2001. Permanent bodies: **Secretariat (Beijing)** and **RATS (Tashkent)**. India & Pakistan joined 2017, Iran 2023.

## QUAD
- **2026 Foreign Ministers' Meeting in New Delhi** (India, USA, Japan, Australia) launched a **Critical Minerals Framework** plus maritime-surveillance and Pacific-port initiatives. QUAD formalised 2007.
keyPoints: 2025 G20 (Johannesburg) was the first held in Africa; 2026 G20 is in Miami, USA (14-15 Dec 2026), chaired by Trump, with South Africa not invited.
India chairs BRICS in 2026, theme 'Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability'; Indonesia joined BRICS in 2025.
SCO 2026 is under China's presidency; its Secretariat is in Beijing and RATS in Tashkent.
The 2026 QUAD Foreign Ministers' Meet in New Delhi launched a Critical Minerals Framework to cut dependence on China.
The African Union became a permanent G20 member during India's 2023 presidency.

items.title: Climate Diplomacy — COP30 Belém & COP31 Antalya
items.body:
## COP30 — Belém, Brazil (2025)
- Held in the Amazon city of **Belém**; India committed to a **more ambitious Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC)**.

## COP31 — Antalya, Turkey (2026)
- The **31st** UN Climate Change Conference, **9-20 November 2026**, at the Antalya Expo Center.
- Host row resolved by compromise: **Turkey hosts**, while **Australia** (minister Chris Bowen) **presides over negotiations**.
- A **pre-COP** and leaders' event were planned in **Fiji/Tuvalu (5-8 October)** to showcase Pacific climate impacts; a World Leaders' Summit is set for Antalya on 11-12 November.
- Next: **COP32 — Addis Ababa (2027)**.

## Frame for MCQs
- COP is the supreme body of the **UNFCCC (1992)**; the **Paris Agreement (2015)** targets limiting warming to well below 2°C, ideally 1.5°C.
- The WMO reported a **91% chance** global temperature will exceed 1.5°C for at least one year in 2026-30.
keyPoints: COP30 (2025) was held at Belém, Brazil; India pledged a more ambitious NDC there.
COP31 (9-20 Nov 2026) is hosted by Turkey at Antalya, with Australia presiding over the negotiations.
COP32 (2027) will be held at Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
The COP is the supreme decision-making body of the UNFCCC (1992); the Paris Agreement dates to 2015.
WMO: 91% chance of a year exceeding 1.5°C warming between 2026 and 2030.
items.source: Wikipedia — 2026 UN Climate Change Conference; factbase ca-2025-12-and-2026-01, ca-2026-06 (F-CA2606-030)

items.title: International Sports 2026 — World Cup & Multi-sport Games
items.body:
## FIFA World Cup 2026
- Co-hosted by **USA, Canada, Mexico**; first with **48 teams** and 104 matches (11 June-19 July 2026).
- **Spain beat Argentina** in the MetLife Stadium (New Jersey) final for its **2nd title** (first since 2010); first WC final with a halftime show. Next edition (2030): Spain-Portugal-Morocco.

## Commonwealth Games 2026 — Glasgow
- Slimmed 10-sport edition (23 July-2 August); **India 4th with 39 medals** (above Scotland on golds); boxing best sport (10 medals, 7 gold).
- **Ahmedabad hosts CWG 2030** (centenary edition); India becomes the 2nd nation after Australia to host twice (after Delhi 2010).

## Asian Games 2026 — Aichi-Nagoya, Japan
- The **20th Asian Games**, 19 September-4 October 2026, motto **'Imagine One Asia'**. Nagoya is Japan's 3rd host after Tokyo (1958) and Hiroshima (1994); marked 75 years since the first Games (New Delhi, 1951). Next: **Doha 2030**.

## Winter Olympics 2026 — Milano-Cortina, Italy
- Hosted across northern Italy (Milan & Cortina d'Ampezzo). France hosts the 2030 Winter Olympics.
keyPoints: 2026 FIFA World Cup: first 48-team edition, co-hosted by USA/Canada/Mexico; Spain beat Argentina for its 2nd title.
CWG 2026 (Glasgow): India finished 4th with 39 medals; Ahmedabad will host the centenary CWG 2030.
2026 Asian Games (20th) were held at Aichi-Nagoya, Japan (19 Sep-4 Oct), motto 'Imagine One Asia'; next is Doha 2030.
2026 Winter Olympics were hosted by Italy (Milano-Cortina).
India first hosted the Asian Games (1951) and the CWG contingent debuted in 1934.

items.title: Nobel Prizes 2025
items.body:
## The six 2025 laureates

| Category | Laureate(s) | For |
|---|---|---|
| Physics | John Clarke, Michel Devoret, John Martinis | Macroscopic quantum tunnelling in electric circuits |
| Chemistry | Susumu Kitagawa, Richard Robson, Omar Yaghi | Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) |
| Medicine | Mary Brunkow, Fred Ramsdell, Shimon Sakaguchi | Peripheral immune tolerance / regulatory T cells |
| Economics | Joel Mokyr, Philippe Aghion, Peter Howitt | Innovation-driven economic growth |
| Literature | László Krasznahorkai (Hungary) | Body of literary work |
| Peace | María Corina Machado (Venezuela) | Democratic rights in Venezuela |

## Exam frame
- The **Peace Prize** is decided in **Oslo** by the **Norwegian Nobel Committee**; the other five are decided in **Sweden** (Stockholm).
- Economics is officially the **Sveriges Riksbank Prize** (since 1969), not one of Alfred Nobel's original prizes.
- **Nobel 2026** laureates are announced in October 2026 (after early October); if unannounced, rely on the 2025 list.
keyPoints: Nobel Physics 2025: Clarke, Devoret, Martinis (macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits).
Nobel Chemistry 2025: Kitagawa, Robson, Yaghi (metal-organic frameworks/MOFs).
Nobel Medicine 2025: Brunkow, Ramsdell, Sakaguchi (peripheral immune tolerance, regulatory T cells).
Nobel Peace 2025: María Corina Machado (Venezuela); Literature 2025: László Krasznahorkai (Hungary).
The Peace Prize is awarded in Oslo (Norwegian Nobel Committee); the other prizes are decided in Sweden.

items.title: India's Diplomacy & Trade 2025-26
items.body:
## Trade agreements
- **India-UK CETA** in force **15 July 2026**: UK gives zero-duty access to nearly **99% of Indian exports**; the **Double Contribution Convention** extends UK NI exemption for detached Indian workers from 12 to 60 months (benefits 75,000+ professionals).
- India joined the **WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies** as the **123rd member** — the WTO's first environment-focused pact (aquaculture/inland fisheries excluded).

## Bilateral partnerships
| Partner | Outcome (2025-26) |
|---|---|
| New Zealand | Strategic Partnership + 'Roadmap to 2030' (first Indian PM visit in ~4 decades) |
| Indonesia | Joint development of **Sabang Port** (near Strait of Malacca) |
| Japan | **Project UNICORN** — first India-Japan defence co-development (16th summit) |
| Russia | **'Programme 2030 for Strategic Economic Cooperation'** (23rd summit; trade ~USD 68-69 bn) |
| Seychelles | ₹1,250-cr Line of Credit + UPI launch (50 years of ties) |

## Multilateral
- India will contest a **UNSC non-permanent seat for 2028-29** (Tajikistan also contesting the Asia-Pacific seat). The UNSC (1945) has 15 members — 5 permanent (veto) + 10 elected for 2-year terms.
- **CEC of India chairs International IDEA for 2026** (Stockholm-based, est. 1995).
keyPoints: India-UK CETA came into force on 15 July 2026, giving zero-duty UK access to ~99% of Indian exports.
India became the 123rd member of the WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies, the WTO's first sustainability pact.
Key 2025-26 partnerships: NZ Strategic Partnership/Roadmap 2030, Indonesia's Sabang Port, Japan's Project UNICORN, Russia's Programme 2030.
India will contest a UNSC non-permanent seat for 2028-29; the UNSC has 15 members (5 permanent with veto, 10 elected for 2 years).
India's Chief Election Commissioner chairs International IDEA (Stockholm) for 2026.

items.title: Global Indices, Organisations & Geopolitics 2025-26
items.body:
## India in global indices
| Index | India's rank | Publisher |
|---|---|---|
| Global Innovation Index 2025 | 38th (from 81st in 2015) | WIPO |
| Global Terrorism Index 2026 | 13th (Pakistan worst) | IEP, Sydney |
| UN SDG Index 2026 | 94th (score 68.3) | SDSN |
| Global Peace Index 2026 | Iceland No.1 | IEP |
| World Bank income class (FY27) | Lower-Middle-Income | World Bank |

## International organisations (founding / HQ / head 2026)
- **WTO** (1995, Geneva) — Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala; **IMF** (1944 Bretton Woods, Washington) — Kristalina Georgieva; **World Bank** — Ajay Banga; **UN Secretary-General** — António Guterres; **WHO** (1948, Geneva) — Tedros Adhanom.
- **IAEA** (1957, Vienna, Nobel 2005); **WFP** (1961, Rome, Nobel 2020).

## Geopolitics & AI diplomacy
- 2025-26 flashpoints: **Gaza ceasefire** framework, the **Russia-Ukraine war**, and the **2026 Iran war** (which forced cancellation of the football Finalissima). US trade tools: **Section 301** (Trade Act of 1974) and Section 232.
- **IndiaAI Impact Summit (Feb 2026)** — first hosted by a Global South country, 92-nation declaration; China launched the **World AI Cooperation Organization (WAICO)** at Shanghai.
- **Sarnath** inscribed as India's **45th UNESCO World Heritage Site**.
keyPoints: India: GII 2025 = 38th, Global Terrorism Index 2026 = 13th, UN SDG Index 2026 = 94th; still Lower-Middle-Income (World Bank).
Org heads 2026: WTO — Okonjo-Iweala, IMF — Georgieva, World Bank — Ajay Banga, UN SG — Guterres, WHO — Tedros.
IAEA (Vienna, 1957) and WFP (Rome, 1961) are Nobel Peace laureates (2005 and 2020).
US Section 301 (Trade Act of 1974) underpins its tariff actions; 2025-26 saw Gaza, Ukraine and the Iran war.
IndiaAI Impact Summit (Feb 2026) was the first by a Global South nation; China set up WAICO in Shanghai; Sarnath became India's 45th UNESCO site.

items.title: International Timeline — November 2025 to January 2026
items.body:
A month-wise ledger of the biggest international events in the run-up window (grounded in the extracted weekly Current Affairs).

## November 2025
| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| 25 Oct (signed) | **UN Convention Against Cybercrime** opened for signature in **Hanoi**; 72 states signed — first legally binding global cybercrime treaty |
| 12 Nov | **Australia-Indonesia Treaty on Common Security** concluded (builds on 2006 Lombok Treaty); Iceland flags **AMOC collapse** as a national security threat |
| 18 Nov | US designates **Saudi Arabia** a **Major Non-NATO Ally** (first Arab state slated for F-35s) |
| 20 Nov | **7th Colombo Security Conclave**, New Delhi — **Seychelles** admitted full member |
| 22-23 Nov | **G20 Johannesburg Summit** — first on African soil; theme 'Solidarity, Equality & Sustainability'; **ACITI** (Australia-Canada-India) partnership launched |
| Nov | India re-elected to **Codex Executive Committee (Asia)**; India-US **2.2 MTPA LPG** deal for 2026; **UNSC Resolution 2805** on peacebuilding; India-Israel **FTA** first step |

## December 2025
| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| Dec | **Mamady Doumbouya** elected **President of Guinea** (military leader since 2021 coup; 7-year term) |
| Dec | **46th GCC Summit** in **Bahrain**; push for a joint air-defence shield |
| Dec | **Asia Power Index 2025** (Lowy Institute): India **3rd**; **Global AI Vibrancy Index 2025**: India 3rd (US 1st, China 2nd) |
| Dec | Andrej Babiš (**ANO**) returns as **Prime Minister of Czechia** after the 2025 election |

## January 2026
| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| 27 Jan | **16th India-EU Summit**, New Delhi — **FTA negotiations concluded** (begun 2007); 'Comprehensive Strategic Agenda: Towards 2030'; Bharat 6G Alliance-6G-IA MoU |
| Jan | **Henley Passport Index 2026**: India **80th**; India announces first **India-Arab Summit** (New Delhi, Feb 2026) |
| 1 Oct 2025 (in force) | **India-EFTA TEPA** — USD 100 bn EFTA investment pledge over 15 years |
keyPoints: Oct-Nov 2025: 72 nations signed the UN Convention Against Cybercrime in Hanoi — the first binding global cybercrime treaty.
22-23 Nov 2025: G20 Johannesburg was the first on African soil (theme 'Solidarity, Equality & Sustainability'); ACITI (Australia-Canada-India) partnership launched.
Nov 2025: US made Saudi Arabia a Major Non-NATO Ally; Seychelles joined the Colombo Security Conclave; UNSC Resolution 2805 reviewed peacebuilding.
Dec 2025: Mamady Doumbouya elected President of Guinea; 46th GCC Summit in Bahrain; India 3rd in the Asia Power Index 2025.
27 Jan 2026: 16th India-EU Summit concluded FTA talks (begun 2007) and adopted the 'Comprehensive Strategic Agenda: Towards 2030'.
items.source: Extracted weekly CA — November Weeks 2-4, December Weeks 1-3 (2025), January Weeks 2 & 4 (2026)

items.title: International Timeline — February to September 2026
items.body:
Scheduled/announced international milestones and the year's key observances (grounded in host-rotation records, treaty dates and standard UN observances). Use for month-by-month mock coverage.

## Summits & scheduled events
| When | Event |
|---|---|
| Feb 2026 | **IndiaAI Impact Summit** (New Delhi) — first by a Global South nation; **India-Arab Summit** (New Delhi); **World Governments Summit** (Dubai); **Winter Olympics** open at Milano-Cortina, Italy |
| 2026 | **G7 presidency: France** (52nd summit); 2025 was Kananaskis, Canada (51st) |
| 15 Jul 2026 | **India-UK CETA** enters into force (zero-duty on ~99% of Indian exports) |
| 23 Jul-2 Aug | **Commonwealth Games**, Glasgow — India 4th (39 medals) |
| 8 Sep 2026 | **Khalilur Rahman (Bangladesh)** takes over as President of the **81st UNGA session** (from Annalena Baerbock, Germany) |
| 19 Sep-4 Oct | **Asian Games**, Aichi-Nagoya, Japan (20th edition) |
| 9-20 Nov 2026 | **COP31**, Antalya, Turkey (Australia presides over negotiations) |

## Key international days by month
| Date | Day |
|---|---|
| 2 Feb / 21 Feb | World Wetlands Day (Ramsar 1971) / International Mother Language Day (UNESCO) |
| 3 Mar / 8 Mar | World Wildlife Day (CITES 1973) / International Women's Day |
| 7 Apr / 22 Apr | World Health Day (WHO founded 1948) / Earth Day (since 1970) |
| 3 May / 22 May | World Press Freedom Day / International Day of Biological Diversity |
| 5 Jun / 21 Jun | World Environment Day / International Day of Yoga |
| 11 Jul | World Population Day (UNFPA) |
| 12 Aug / 19 Aug | International Youth Day / World Humanitarian Day (2003 Baghdad bombing) |
| 8 Sep / 16 Sep / 21 Sep | International Literacy Day / World Ozone Day (Montreal Protocol 1987) / International Day of Peace |

## Ongoing environment negotiations
- **Global Plastics Treaty**: the INC process (UNEA 2022 mandate, under UNEP) works towards a legally binding instrument on plastic pollution.
keyPoints: Feb 2026 clusters four flagships: IndiaAI Impact Summit, India-Arab Summit, World Governments Summit (Dubai) and the Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics.
France holds the 2026 G7 presidency (52nd summit); the 2025 summit was at Kananaskis, Canada.
8 Sep 2026: Khalilur Rahman (Bangladesh) becomes President of the 81st UNGA session, succeeding Annalena Baerbock (Germany).
Key days: World Health Day 7 Apr (WHO, 1948), Yoga Day 21 Jun, World Ozone Day 16 Sep (Montreal Protocol, 1987), Peace Day 21 Sep.
The Global Plastics Treaty is being negotiated via the INC under UNEP's 2022 UNEA mandate.

items.title: Exam-Precision: SCO Tianjin, M23/DRC & the 18th BRICS Summit
items.body:
## Summits

- The **SCO Heads-of-State Summit 2025** was hosted by **China at Tianjin**.
- The **18th BRICS Summit (2026)** is hosted by **India in New Delhi**; India holds the BRICS chair from **1 January 2026**.

## Conflict

- The **M23 rebels** are active in **Eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC)** - part of the Great Lakes region conflict, with recurring seizures of territory in North Kivu.
keyPoints: The SCO Heads-of-State Summit 2025 was hosted by China at Tianjin.
The 18th BRICS Summit (2026) is hosted by India in New Delhi.
The M23 rebels operate in Eastern DRC as part of the Great Lakes conflict.
